title: A limit over a cofiltered category is a limit over a directed set (Stacks 0032)
statement: Let $\mathcal I$ be a small cofiltered category, $\mathcal C$ a category, $D:\mathcal I\to\mathcal C$ a functor and $(S,(\pi_x:S\to D(x))_{x\in\mathcal I})$ a limit cone of $D$ (a limit in $\mathcal C$ is a colimit in $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every family $g_x:T\to D(x)$ with $D(a)\circ g_x=g_y$ for all $a:x\to y$ there is exactly one $u:T\to S$ with $\pi_x\circ u=g_x$ for all $x$). Then there are a nonempty directed set $(A,\le)$, objects $x_a\in\mathcal I$ ($a\in A$) and morphisms $\varphi_{ba}:x_b\to x_a$ ($a\le b$) with $\varphi_{aa}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi_{ba}\circ\varphi_{cb}=\varphi_{ca}$ ($a\le b\le c$), such that $(S,(\pi_{x_a})_{a\in A})$ is a limit of the inverse system $(D(x_a),D(\varphi_{ba}))$ over $A$. In particular, if every $D(x)$ has a property and every $D(a)$ is of a class of morphisms, then so are the terms $D(x_a)$ and transition maps $D(\varphi_{ba})$ of the inverse system.
